structured_output.justification: The pricing trace correctly applies the contract: consignment FF-8005 (SH-4005) has a billed weight of 260 kg, which falls squarely in the "up to and including 500 kg" band at ₹18.00/km (§1), over a booked distance of 800 km, giving a base freight of 14,400. The express service premium of 15% on base freight (§2) and the 12% fuel surcharge on base-plus-express (§3) are both correctly computed and compounded in the order the contract specifies, yielding an expected freight charge that is fully reconciled from the shipment facts and rate card with no unresolved band boundary, no missing accessorial trigger (special_handling is empty, so residential delivery under §4 correctly did not fire), and no ambiguity in weight banding (260 kg is not near the 500/501 kg boundary noted as ambiguous elsewhere in this rate card). The billed amount exceeds this correctly-traced expected amount by a determinable margin, which is a straightforward overcharge relative to the contract's own freight formula rather than a defensible alternate reading of any clause.

memo_narrative.what_happened: Falcon billed consignment FF-8005 above the amount the contract's freight formula (base per-km rate by weight band, plus express premium and fuel surcharge) produces for this 260 kg, 800 km, express shipment.
memo_narrative.why: The weight band, express premium, and fuel surcharge are each correctly and unambiguously determined under §1, §2, and §3, with no boundary or trigger ambiguity for this consignment, so the amount above the contract-derived figure is an unsupported overcharge.
memo_narrative.recommended_action: Raise a billing dispute with Falcon citing §1-§3 and request a corrected invoice for FF-8005 reflecting the contract-derived freight charge.
